text: Ship stores sold to landsmen at landsman prices.
Twine, hooks, tar, and a barrel of biscuit that has outlasted
two owners of this shop and shows no sign of stopping.
Vessels stacked in rope cradles so they cannot roll.
The wall behind them is salt-stained to knee height from the
spring the harbour came up over the sill.
Lamp oil, in every size of can there is.
Tideglass burns a great deal of lamp oil. The fog does not
care what hour it is, and neither does the light on the mole.
The display case, its glass gone soft and wavy with age.
Tonics inside, arranged by colour rather than by use,
which the clerk insists is a system.
